summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, cough, and shortness of breath two days after potential sick contact. Initial chest X-ray showed subtle right middle lobe changes, prompting empiric treatment with ceftriaxone and azithromycin for possible pneumonia. Nasal swab confirmed RSV infection, and CT scan revealed diffuse bronchial wall thickening and ground-glass opacities consistent with viral bronchiolitis, without focal consolidation. Ceftriaxone was discontinued, and he completed a short course of azithromycin. His blood counts dropped during admission, likely due to RSV or medications, but showed signs of recovery by discharge. He remained stable on room air, with normal oxygen saturation, and returned to his baseline health. He was discharged home with instructions to continue his regular medications, complete azithromycin, use albuterol as needed, and follow up for CBC and INR monitoring.
problems: Pneumonia due to respiratory syncytial virus
